note: SNAPSHOT. Every number below was correct on catalog_version and is stale the moment a vendor changes a price or ships a model. Regenerating this file is the REQ-CAT-06 ritual, and two fields must be diffed per model on every regeneration because they change the request body: thinking_level_map (REQ-PROV-15 -- an entry that silently disappears turns a clamped request into a 400, and an entry that silently appears sends a level the model does not know) and cost, including the vendor of fallback-served rows (REQ-PROV-05.5 -- dropping it bills a fallback at the wrong rate, silently). Everything else in a row is a capability hint the clamp and the budget gate can survive being slightly wrong about. This catalog is NOT an allowlist: an unknown id under a known vendor clones that vendor's default_model row (REQ-CAT-03), so a model released after this snapshot works without an SDK release. Two vendor-wide facts that do not fit in a row: (1) all three vendors have moved their reasoning control from a token budget to a discrete level -- output_config.effort on Anthropic, reasoning_effort on OpenAI, thinkingLevel on Gemini. The Anthropic and OpenAI adapters emit their vendor's current field: on an anthropic row an INTEGER wire value is a budget_tokens and an effort TOKEN (low..max) is sent as output_config.effort with adaptive thinking, and a row that rejects temperature/top_p says so with compat.supports_sampling false. The google adapter does not yet speak thinkingLevel, so its rows record levels as PRESENT-AND-NULL: checked, and not expressible on the wire this SDK sends. Present-null and absent are runtime-identical (ruling P-28); the runtime effect of a fully null ladder is that the thinking parameter is omitted, which on every such row means the vendor's own default, never a 400. An `off` entry that is present-and-null means the model cannot stop thinking and the anthropic adapter omits the key for a request of off rather than sending a rejected disable. (2) The google rows are the AI Studio deployment; Vertex AI is the same wire behind a different host and credential and is selected by configuration (Options.VertexProject or a Vertex base URL), never by a catalog row.

claude-fable-5-1.name: Claude Fable 5.1
claude-fable-5-1.note: Thinking is always on and cannot be disabled: `off` is present-and-null, so the adapter omits the thinking key ({"type":"disabled"} is a 400 here). Every other level is an output_config.effort token sent with {"type":"adaptive"}; budget_tokens is rejected on this model, and so are temperature/top_p (compat.supports_sampling false drops them). Forced tool_choice any/tool is also a 400; the adapter only sends auto/none. Cache read is 0.025x input on this row -- a quarter of the 0.1x every other Anthropic row charges. Cache write is the 5-minute rate (1.25x input); a 1h write is priced by provider.ComputeCost, not from this row.

claude-fable-5.name: Claude Fable 5
claude-fable-5.note: Predecessor of claude-fable-5-1 at the same per-token price and the same always-on thinking: `off` is present-and-null (disabled is a 400), levels are effort tokens with adaptive thinking, budget_tokens and temperature/top_p are rejected. The one billing difference is cache read at the standard 0.1x input rather than Fable 5.1's 0.025x.

claude-opus-5-5.name: Claude Opus 5.5
claude-opus-5-5.note: Thinking is always on and cannot be disabled: `off` is present-and-null, so the adapter omits the thinking key ({"type":"disabled"} is a 400, as is budget_tokens -- both probed against the API on 2026-09-30, and the migration guide says the same). Every other level is an output_config.effort token sent with {"type":"adaptive"}; default effort is medium. temperature/top_p/top_k are 400s (compat.supports_sampling false). Forced tool_choice any/tool is also a 400; the adapter only sends auto/none. Priced at $4/$20, below Opus 5's $5/$25. Cache write is the 5-minute rate ($5 = 1.25x input; 1h is $8 and is priced by provider.ComputeCost); cache read is $0.20 = 0.05x input. 1M context at one price, so no tiers. Released 2026-09-22; retirement not sooner than 2027-09-22.

claude-opus-5.name: Claude Opus 5
claude-opus-5.note: Effort-style row: every level above off is an output_config.effort token sent with {"type":"adaptive"}. Omitting the key also means adaptive on this model (thinking is on by default), and `off` is "disabled", which the model accepts only at effort high or below -- the adapter sends no effort alongside disabled, so the default (high) applies. budget_tokens and temperature/top_p are 400s here (compat.supports_sampling false). Cache write is the 5-minute rate (1.25x input); cache read is 0.1x input.

claude-opus-4-8.name: Claude Opus 4.8
claude-opus-4-8.note: Same request surface as claude-opus-4-7: effort tokens with adaptive thinking, `off` is "disabled", budget_tokens and temperature/top_p are 400s. Unlike Opus 5, omitting the thinking key means NO thinking on this model, which is why every level above off must be sent explicitly as adaptive.

claude-opus-4-7.name: Claude Opus 4.7
claude-opus-4-7.note: The generation that removed budget_tokens and the sampling parameters and introduced the xhigh effort: levels are effort tokens with adaptive thinking, `off` is "disabled", temperature/top_p are 400s (compat.supports_sampling false). Omitting the thinking key means no thinking here.

claude-opus-4-6.name: Claude Opus 4.6
claude-opus-4-6.note: First adaptive-thinking generation: levels are effort tokens sent with {"type":"adaptive"} and `off` is "disabled". xhigh is ABSENT -- it arrived with Opus 4.7 -- so a request for xhigh clamps UP to max (REQ-PROV-15). budget_tokens still works but is deprecated and this adapter never sends it to an effort row; temperature/top_p are still accepted.

claude-sonnet-5-5.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
claude-sonnet-5-5.note: Adaptive thinking is on by default. `off` is present-and-null because {"type":"disabled"} is a 400 on this model (probed 2026-09-30) -- unlike Sonnet 5, which still accepts it. The vendor's replacement is {"type":"between_tools"}, which skips up-front thinking (works at effort high or below); the adapter does not send it, so a request for `off` omits the thinking key and the model thinks at its default. Every other level is an output_config.effort token sent with {"type":"adaptive"}; budget_tokens is a 400 and so is any temperature/top_p/top_k (compat.supports_sampling false). Forced tool_choice any/tool is a 400; the adapter only sends auto/none. Same $2/$10 and cache rates as Sonnet 5; cache write is the 5-minute rate ($2.50 = 1.25x input; 1h is $4). 1M context at one price, so no tiers. Released 2026-09-28; retirement not sooner than 2027-09-28.

claude-sonnet-5.name: Claude Sonnet 5
claude-sonnet-5.note: Vendor default_model: the clone template for unknown anthropic ids, and therefore the row an id released after this snapshot inherits its window, cap, price and effort-style ladder from. Levels are effort tokens with adaptive thinking, `off` is "disabled", budget_tokens and temperature/top_p are 400s (compat.supports_sampling false). $2/$10 is the standard rate; the once-scheduled rise to $3/$15 did not happen. 1M context at one price -- no long-context tier, which is why cost.tiers is absent here and present on every openai row.

claude-sonnet-4-6.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
claude-sonnet-4-6.note: Same ladder and rules as claude-opus-4-6 one tier down: effort tokens with adaptive thinking, `off` is "disabled", no xhigh (clamps up to max), temperature/top_p accepted, budget_tokens deprecated and never sent by this adapter.

claude-opus-4-5.name: Claude Opus 4.5
claude-opus-4-5.note: Budget-wire row: the values are thinking token budgets for {"type":"enabled","budget_tokens":N}, 1024 is the vendor minimum, and `off` is "disabled". xhigh and max are ABSENT, so a request for either clamps DOWN to high. 200k window and 64k output cap -- a sibling clone of the default_model would get 1M/128k and be wrong about this one. Lifecycle: active but legacy; the vendor's tentative retirement is not sooner than 2026-11-24 (checked 2026-09-30) -- the row stays until the API stops serving the id.

claude-sonnet-4-5.name: Claude Sonnet 4.5
claude-sonnet-4-5.note: Budget-wire row like claude-opus-4-5: token budgets, 1024 minimum, `off` is "disabled", xhigh/max absent and clamped down to high. 200k window, 64k output cap. output_config.effort is an error on this model, which is why the ladder is budgets and not tokens. Lifecycle: active but legacy; the vendor's tentative retirement is not sooner than 2026-09-29 (checked 2026-09-30) -- the row stays until the API stops serving the id.

claude-haiku-4-5.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
claude-haiku-4-5.note: The smallest current row and a budget-wire one: the values are thinking token budgets, 1024 is the vendor minimum, `off` is "disabled". xhigh and max are ABSENT rather than null -- nothing was checked, they are opt-in -- so a request for max clamps DOWN to high, REQ-PROV-15's worked example. 200k window and 64k cap; output_config.effort is an error here, so the ladder stays in budgets. Lifecycle: active but legacy; the vendor's tentative retirement is not sooner than 2026-10-15 (checked 2026-09-30) -- the row stays until the API stops serving the id.

gpt-6-astra.name: GPT-6 Astra
gpt-6-astra.note: The flagship, and the row where every REQ-PROV-15 shape appears at once. `off` is present-and-null: reasoning_effort:"none" is a 400 on Astra alone (the gpt-5.6 rows accept it), and recording that explicitly is what lets the REQ-CAT-06 diff tell a checked fact from an unfilled row -- it changes nothing at runtime, since the adapter returns before the clamp for off. `minimal` is present-and-null because this ladder starts at low, so a request for minimal clamps UP. compat keys are the openai-completions profile's OWN json names (provider/openai.Compat, REQ-PROV-12) and that profile rejects any key it does not read at request time: supports_temperature false because Astra rejects temperature and top_p, and use_max_tokens is left at the profile default (false -> max_completion_tokens) because gpt-5.x and later reject max_tokens outright. Cache read is 0.1x input and cache write is 1.25x input on this generation -- the free cache write of the gpt-4o era is gone, and a row that kept the old 0.0 would under-bill every cached prefix.

gpt-6.1-sol.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
gpt-6.1-sol.note: Near-Astra quality at $2/$10. THIS ROW OVERRIDES THE VENDOR'S WIRE: api is openai-responses, not the vendor default openai-completions, because the model page says tool calling needs the Responses API and Chat Completions is supported only without tool calling -- an agent on the completions wire would lose every tool. compat keys are therefore the openai-responses profile's own names (provider/openairesponses.Compat): supports_sampling_params false because reasoning models on this wire reject temperature and top_p; the other flags are left at the api.openai.com defaults. The vendor documents reasoning.effort as low, medium (default), high, xhigh and max only -- `none` and `minimal` are not supported, so both are present-and-null and a request for minimal clamps UP to low (never to off). Cached input is 0.05x input ($0.10) and cache writes are 1.25x ($2.50). The tier is REQ-PROV-05.4: a request over 272,000 input tokens is repriced whole at 2x input/cache and 1.5x output.

gpt-5.6-sol.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
gpt-5.6-sol.note: `off` is "none" here -- this family CAN be told not to reason, unlike Astra -- and it is recorded even though the adapter never sends reasoning_effort for off, because the fact is what the diff needs. A promotional $4/$20 ran through at least 2026-11-21; the STANDARD rate is what this row carries, so the REQ-LOOP-08 budget gate over-estimates rather than under-estimates while the promotion lasts. The tier is REQ-PROV-05.4: a request whose input + cache tokens EXCEED 272,000 is repriced whole -- output included, at 1.5x -- not just the tokens past the threshold.

gpt-5.6-terra.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
gpt-5.6-terra.note: Vendor default_model: the clone template for unknown openai ids. It is the middle of the range on purpose (REQ-CAT-03's documented guess is wrong least often in the middle), which also means an unknown id that is really a nano-class model inherits Terra's price and is over-billed by the estimate rather than under-billed.

gpt-6-luna.name: GPT-6 Luna
gpt-6-luna.note: The GPT-6 efficiency tier at $0.10/$0.50, cheaper than gpt-5.6-luna. THIS ROW OVERRIDES THE VENDOR'S WIRE: api is openai-responses, because the model page says built-in tools and function calling belong to the Responses API and Chat Completions supports function calling only with reasoning_effort set to none -- a completions row would silently lose tools at any other level. compat keys are the openai-responses profile's own names: supports_sampling_params false (reasoning models reject temperature and top_p); everything else stays at the api.openai.com default. reasoning.effort accepts none, low, medium (default), high, xhigh and max; `minimal` is present-and-null, so a request for minimal clamps UP to low. `off` is "none" and is recorded although the adapter never sends reasoning for off. Cached input is 0.1x input ($0.01) and cache writes are 1.25x ($0.125). The tier is REQ-PROV-05.4: over 272,000 input tokens the whole request is repriced at 2x input/cache and 1.5x output.

gpt-5.6-luna.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
gpt-5.6-luna.note: The high-volume tier: cut 80% on 2026-07-30, from $1/$6 to $0.20/$1.20. A price that moved that far in one step is the reason cost is one of the two fields REQ-CAT-06 makes mandatory to diff.

gemini-3.1-pro-preview.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
gemini-3.1-pro-preview.note: Gemini 3.x replaced the integer thinkingBudget with the thinkingLevel enum (LOW or HIGH on the Pro line). The numeric field survives only as a backward-compatible alias, the two may not be sent together, and no per-level budget is published for this family -- so every level is present-and-null: checked, and not expressible as the number resolveThinking would have to send. The adapter therefore omits thinkingConfig entirely, which is this model's documented dynamic default. Thinking cannot be turned off at all, so can_disable_thinking is false and `off` degrades to min_thinking_budget, recorded as -1: Gemini's own "dynamic" budget, and the only value that is not a rejected request on a family that will not stop thinking. cache_write is 0.0 because Google bills context caching by storage-hour rather than by written token -- a dimension this catalog does not model, so a heavily cached run is under-estimated by the storage fee and by nothing else. The id carries the -preview suffix the vendor still ships it under; dropping the suffix resolves to a sibling clone of gemini-3.8-flash and mis-prices the request by 2.7x. Prompts over 200,000 tokens reprice the whole request (REQ-PROV-05.4).

gemini-3.8-flash.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
gemini-3.8-flash.note: Vendor default_model: the clone template for unknown google ids, and the middle of the current range. Thinking levels the vendor documents are low, medium (default) and high, and MINIMAL is a validation error; this row records a present-and-null ladder because the adapter does not speak thinkingLevel, so the thinking parameter is omitted except for `off`. Unlike the Pro row, this model CAN stop thinking: the API accepts thinkingBudget 0 and returns no thought tokens (probed 2026-09-30), so the row carries no can_disable_thinking/min_thinking_budget entries and the adapter's defaults apply -- `off` sends thinkingBudget 0. An earlier snapshot recorded can_disable_thinking false with a -1 floor, which made `off` degrade to dynamic thinking and bill thought tokens the caller had asked not to buy. THIS ROW'S PRICE EXPIRES: $0.75/$3.75 is introductory pricing through 2026-12-31 and becomes $1.50/$7.50 (cache read $0.15) on 2027-01-01, which the next REQ-CAT-06 regeneration must pick up -- an expired introductory rate under-bills by exactly 2x and nothing in the request will say so. Thinking tokens bill at the output rate here and never appear in the response body.

gemini-3.7-flash.name: Gemini 3.7 Flash
gemini-3.7-flash.note: Previous-generation Flash, stable. Vendor thinking levels: low, medium (default), high. THIS ROW'S PRICE EXPIRES: $0.75/$3.75 (cache read $0.075) is introductory pricing through 2026-12-31 and becomes $1.50/$7.50 (cache read $0.15) on 2027-01-01, which the next REQ-CAT-06 regeneration must pick up -- an expired introductory rate under-bills by exactly 2x and nothing in the request will say so. Same present-and-null ladder as the rows above: the adapter does not speak thinkingLevel, so the thinking parameter is sent only for `off` (thinkingBudget 0, which this model accepts -- probed 2026-09-30: zero thought tokens, no error; no compat entry is needed because can_disable_thinking defaults to true) and is otherwise omitted, leaving the vendor's default. cache_write is 0.0 because Google bills caching by storage-hour, which the catalog does not model.

gemini-3.1-flash-lite.note: Stable lite tier, cheaper than gemini-3.5-flash-lite. Prices are the text/image/video rate; audio input is $0.50 (cache $0.05), a dimension this catalog does not model.
